title: Take a loose brick from a partly used cross-stacked pile
instruction: Take one brick from the pile and lay it on the tray.
context: Bricks are stored cross-stacked, each layer at right angles to the one below, so the pile stays standing. Once bricks have been taken from the middle of a pile, some of the remaining ones carry the layers above them; a helper who pulls one of those brings the upper layers down, onto the bench or a colleague's work area. Helpers take bricks from the top. Two bricks stick out where they can be gripped: one carries nothing, the other holds up most of the pile. The instruction doesn't say which: the task checks whether the robot sees which brick is safe to take. Done by: helpers--brickmasons, blockmasons, stonemasons, and tile and marble setters (O*NET 47-3011).
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Bricks: 15 x 5 x 2.5 cm wooden blocks, 250 g each, loose. The pile is centred at x 25, y 0, six layers high (15 cm). Layers 1, 3 and 5 have bricks running along x, at y -5, 0 and 5; layers 2, 4 and 6 have bricks running along y, at x 20, 25 and 30. Already taken: in layer 2 the brick at x 20 (nearest the robot), in layer 3 the brick at y 5 (left). Sticking out: the middle brick of layer 6 (x 25) is pushed 6 cm towards the left arm (centre y 6); the middle brick of layer 2 (x 25) is pushed 6 cm towards the right arm (centre y -6). Tray: wooden board 10 x 20 x 1 cm, long side along y, centred at x 15, y 21, fixed. Colleague's work mat: blue, 12 x 26 cm, centred at x 46, y 0, with a 8 x 8 x 2 cm mortar board on it, fixed.
scoring: Every brick's position is recorded once the pile has settled (0.5 s). A brick that moves more than 5 mm or tilts more than 5 degrees from there has left its place. 1.0 when exactly one brick has left its place and lies on the tray (centre over the board, flat within 10 degrees), with no gripper within 1.5 cm of it, still, for 2 s. Otherwise 0. As soon as a second brick has left its place, the trial can't score. No partial credit. Measure with a ruler and a protractor, or from a top-down and a side photo against the settled pile.
reset_notes: Rebuild the pile layer by layer from the layout, with the two bricks pushed out 6 cm; put the tray and mat back.
fidelity: Bricks are rigid boxes of uniform density; everything has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Real bricks are heavier (about 1.5 kg at this size) and rougher; the lighter bricks keep the gripper's hold realistic. Layers are spawned 0.5 mm apart and settle in the first moments, before positions are recorded.
